recipes.reason: Vendor table includes Laguna and Inkling on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Pro. Use the lower comparator without a benchmark-version conversion.

sources.summary: Laguna exceeds Inkling on the reported shared coding tests. Harness differences and transfer to AA v10 roles remain uncertain.

recipes.reason: Official blind engineering comparison with GLM 5.3 supports only coding-role analogies, without claiming general reasoning or factuality equivalence.

sources.summary: 203 engineering tasks, 163 internal experts; average 2.99 versus GLM 5.3 at 2.92. Vendor evaluation, not AA.

recipes.reason: Vendor table compares coding, SciCode and agentic tasks with the observed anchors. Use their minimum with a wide haircut; keep all raw target benchmark fields absent.

sources.summary: Developer-reported TerminalBench 2.1, SWE-bench and SciCode comparisons; CyberGym is not Cyber Index and is never transferred.

recipes.reason: Preserve exact AA target LCR/HLE/SciCode contributions. Only missing role contributions use low-capability observed coding anchors with a wide policy margin; vendor TB2.1 is never substituted for AA TB4.

sources.summary: Exact high-effort target has observed LCR, HLE, SciCode and legacy Terminal-Bench; no v5 Intelligence.
Vendor reports SWE-bench Pro 56.3 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 at 59.5. These establish coding relevance, not metric equivalence.
Low-tier coding reference table includes Inkling TB2.1 63.8 and Nemotron 3 Ultra 56.4. Harness differences require a wide policy range.

recipes.reason: Exact non-reasoning AA target measurements stay intact. Later Haiku is only a same-line upper reference with a 45-point haircut for missing contributions; no reasoning-effort score is copied into the non-reasoning row.

sources.summary: Exact non-reasoning target has observed HLE and LCR; other core fields and Intelligence v5 remain absent.
Official Terminal-Bench footnote distinguishes no-thinking 40.21 and thinking 41.75, with 11 runs in total. Other coding headlines use extended thinking and cannot be transferred as observations.

recipes.reason: Independent mathematics/science evaluations support a narrow hard-question-answering analogy only. Lower-scoring target GPQA and unvalidated cross-task transfer receive a wide haircut; no coding or professional-deliverable score is inferred.

sources.summary: Epoch publishes GPQA 82.323% thinking and 80.808% no-thinking, FrontierMath tiers1-3 v2 19.298%, OTIS mock AIME and game results, with execution logs.
Independent ground-truth vision tests: 52.4 overall, reasoning low/high 34.4/61.6. Single run per task; these remain diagnostics rather than AA role observations.
Exact catalog route qwen/qwen3.7-flash; no AA score is asserted.

recipes.reason: Nine published task results include SVG construction and sequential games. Only a weak normal-implementation analogy is permitted; hidden provider identity is not guessed, and no broad intelligence, heavy-agent or security measurement is asserted.

sources.summary: StealthMark 18.9, General12.0, Visual29.8 across 7 SVG tasks and 2 games, with per-task artifacts. Small task suite and evaluator subjectivity limit transfer.

recipes.reason: Use the original June launch technical report as an explicitly uncertain coding analogy to its frontier reference class. The unversioned catalog route is verified, but the current revision is unconfirmed; v2 results are not imported. Anchor Intelligence v5 is unavailable, so portfolios remain blocked.

sources.summary: Original report: Ultra SWE-bench Pro73.7, TB2.1 82.1, SciCode58.7, HLE50.0 and LCR73.3; comparisons include Fable5/Mythos and an Opus4.8/GPT5.5/Gemini3.1 worker pool. Preserve that revision.
June23 catalog launch establishes sakana/fugu-ultra route and 1M context. It does not verify the current serving revision.
Later official v1.1 improves coding benchmarks by up to7.9 points. This verifies version drift rather than equivalence to the unversioned route.
